title: Only 51 Kakapo Were Left. Now They're in a Record Baby Boom

scenes.text: Only 51 of these parrots were left in 1995.
It's the kakapo, the heaviest parrot on Earth, up to nine pounds, and it can't really fly.
It smells fruity, which made it easy prey for animals that hunt by scent.
And it only breeds when rimu trees give a huge crop of fruit, every two to four years.
This year the trees delivered. Nearly every mature female bred, and they laid 256 eggs.
From 51 birds to about 235 today. Watch the comeback again.

description:
Only 51 kakapo were left in 1995.
The flightless, fruity-smelling parrot only breeds when rimu trees produce a bumper crop. In 2026, nearly every mature female bred and laid 256 eggs, a record season, taking the wild population to about 235.
Would you help save the kakapo? Comment below.
